transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have, I have.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First question is what’s in the best interests of the United States?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What’s in the best interests of our people?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When it comes to foreign policy that will be my guiding question.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Is it in our nation’s interests?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Peace in the Middle East is in our nation’s interests.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Having a hemisphere that is free for trade and peaceful is in our nation’s interests.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Strong relations in Europe is in our nation’s interest.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve thought a lot about what it means to be the president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I also understand that an administration is not one person, but an administration is dedicated citizens who are called by the president to serve the country, to serve a cause greater than self, and so I’ve thought about an administration of people who represent all America, but people who understand my compassionate and conservative philosophy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I haven’t started naming names except for one person, and that’s Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Richard Cheney who I thought did a great job the other night.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s a vice presidential nominee who represents — I think people got to see why I picked him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s man of solid judgment and he’s going to be a person to stand by my side.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One of the things I’ve done in Texas is I’ve been able to put together a good team of people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been able to set clear goals.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The goals ought to be an education system that leaves no child behind, Medicare for our seniors, a Social Security system that’s safe and secure, foreign policy that’s in our nation’s interest, and a strong military, and then bring people together to achieve those goals.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what a Chief Executive Officer does.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I’ve thought long and hard about the honor of being the President of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Yes, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’ve thought a lot about that particular question, and I see our greatest national strength coming from what we stand for in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I see it as a question of values.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It is a great tribute to our founders that 224 years later this nation is now looked to by the peoples on every other continent and the peoples from every part of this earth as a kind of model for what their future could be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t think that’s just the kind of exaggeration that we take pride in as Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s really true, even the ones that sometimes shake their fists at us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: As soon as they have a change that allows the people to speak freely, they’re wanting to develop some kind of blueprint that will help them be like us more, freedom, free markets, political freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So I think first and foremost our power ought to be wielded to in ways that form a more perfect union.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The power of example is America’s greatest power in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And that means, for example, standing up for human rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It means addressing the problems of injustice and inequity, along the lines of race and ethnicity here at home, because in all these other places around the world where they’re having these terrible problems, when they feel hope, it is often because they see in us a reflection of their potential.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve got to enforce our civil rights laws.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to deal with things like racial profiling.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And we have to keep our military strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have the strongest military, and I’ll do whatever is necessary, if I’m president, to make sure that it stays that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But our real power comes, I think, from our values.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think they ought to look at us as a country that understands freedom where it doesn’t matter who you are or how you’re raised or where you’re from, that you can succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think they’ll look at us with envy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It really depends upon how our nation conducts itself in foreign policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If we’re an arrogant nation, they’ll resent us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If we’re a humble nation, but strong, they’ll welcome us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s — our nation stands alone right now in the world in terms of power, and that’s why we have to be humble.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And yet project strength in a way that promotes freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I don’t think they ought to look at us in any way other than what we are.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re a freedom-loving nation and if we’re an arrogant nation they’ll view us that way, but if we’re a humble nation they’ll respect us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I agree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I agree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that one of the problems that we have faced in the world is that we are so much more powerful than any single nation has been in relationship to the rest of the world than at any time in history, that I know about, anyway.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That there is some resentment of U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: power.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So I think that the idea of humility is an important one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I think that we also have to have a sense of mission in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have to protect our capacity to push forward what America’s all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That means not only military strength and our values, it also means keeping our economy strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You know, in the last, or two decades ago, it was routine for leaders of foreign countries to come over here and say you guys have got to do something about these horrendous deficits because it’s causing tremendous problems for the rest of the world, and we were lectured to all the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The fact that we have the strongest economy in history today is not good enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We need to do more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But the fact that it is so strong enables us to project the power for good that America can represent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, it does.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Take, for example, Third World debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to be forgiving Third World debt under certain conditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think, for example, if we’re convinced that a Third World country that’s got a lot of debt would reform itself, that the money wouldn’t go into the hands of a few but would go to help people, I think it makes sense for us to use our wealth in that way, or to trade debt for valuable rain forest lands, makes that much sense, yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We do have an obligation, but we can’t be all things to all people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can help build coalitions but we can’t put our troops all around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can lend money but we have to do it wisely.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We shouldn’t be lending money to corrupt officials.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So we got to be guarded in our generosity.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And therefore, the term honest broker makes sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This current administration’s worked hard to keep the parties at the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I will try to do the same thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it won’t be on my timetable, it will be on the timetable that people are comfortable with in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.text: I haven’t heard a big difference in the last few exchanges.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s hard to tell.

transcript_turns.text: I think that, you know, I would hope to be able to convince people I could handle the Iraqi situation better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would like to, of course, and I presume this administration would as well.

transcript_turns.text: We don’t know — there are no inspectors now in Iraq, the coalition that was in place isn’t as strong as it used to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He is a danger.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Some of them I’ve got a conflict of interest on, if you know what I mean.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the administration did the right thing in that case.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was a horrible situation, no one liked to see it on our TV screens, but it’s a case where we need to make sure we have an early warning system in place in places where there could be ethnic cleansing and genocide the way we saw it there in Rwanda.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s a case where we need to use our influence to have countries in Africa come together and help deal with the situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The administration, seems like we’re having a great love fest tonight, but the administration made the right decision on training Nigerian troops for situations just such as this in Rwanda, and so I thought they made the right decision not to send U.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: troops into Rwanda.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to come back to the question of nation building, but let me address the question directly, first.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Fine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We did, actually, send troops into Rwanda to help with the humanitarian relief measures.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: My wife Tipper, who is here, actually went on a military plane with General Sholicatchvieli on one of those flights.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I think in retrospect we were too late getting in there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We could have saved more lives if we had acted earlier.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I do not think that it was an example of a conflict where we should have put our troops in to try to separate the parties for this reason, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: One of the criteria that I think is important in deciding when and if we should ever get involved around the world is whether or not our national security interest is involved, if we can really make the difference with military forces.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If we tried everything else, if we have allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In the Balkans we have allies, NATO, ready, willing and able to go and carry a big part of the burden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In Africa we did not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, we have tried — our country has tried to create an Africa crisis response team there, and we’ve met some resistance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have had some luck with Nigeria, but in Sierra Leon, and now that Nigeria has become a democracy, and we hope it stays that way, then maybe we can build on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But because we had no allies and because it was very unclear that we could actually accomplish what we would want to accomplish about putting military forces there, I think it was the right thing not to jump in, as heartbreaking as it was, but I think we should have come in much quicker with the humanitarian mission.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I understand, and Africa is important.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to do a lot of work in Africa to promote democracy and trade, and there are some — Vice President mentioned Nigeria is a fledgling democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have to work with Nigeria.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Itâ€™s an important continent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But there’s got to be priorities, and Middle East is a priority for a lot of reasons, as is Europe and the Far East, our own hemisphere.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And those are my four top priorities should I be the president, not to say we won’t be engaged nor work hard to get other nations to come together to prevent atrocity.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I thought the best example of a way to handle the situation was East Timor when we provided logistical support to the Australians, support that only we can provide.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I thought that was a good model.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we can’t be all things to all people in the world, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think that’s where maybe the vice president and I begin to have some differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m worried about overcommitting our military around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to be judicious in its use.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You mentioned Haiti.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I wouldn’t have sent troops to Haiti.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t think it was a mission worthwhile.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was a nation building mission, and it was not very successful.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It cost us billions, a couple billions of dollars, and I’m not so sure democracy is any better off in Haiti than it was before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we agree on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I would certainly also be judicious in evaluating any potential use of American troops overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think we have to be very reticent about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But look, Jim, the world is changing so rapidly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The way I see it, the world is getting much closer together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Like it or not, we are now — the United States is now the natural leader of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: All these other countries are looking to us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, just because we cannot be involved everywhere, and shouldn’t be, doesn’t mean that we should shy away from going in anywhere.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, both of us are kind of, I guess, stating the other’s position in a maximalist extreme way, but I think there is a difference here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: This idea of nation building is kind of a pejorative phrase, but think about the great conflict of the past century, World War II.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: During the years between World War I and World War II, a great lesson was learned by our military leaders and the people of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The lesson was that in the aftermath of World War I, we kind of turned our backs and left them to their own devices and they brewed up a lot of trouble that quickly became World War II.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And acting upon that lesson in the aftermath of our great victory in World War II, we laid down the Marshall Plan, President Truman did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We got intimately involved in building NATO and other structures there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We still have lots of troops in Europe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And what did we do in the late ’40’s and ’50’s and ’60’s?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We were nation building.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And it was economic.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But it was also military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the confidence that those countries recovering from the wounds of war had by having troops there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We had civil administrators come in to set up their ways of building their towns back.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First let me just say one comment about what the vice president said.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think one of the lessons in between World War I and World War II is we let our military atrophy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we can’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to rebuild our military.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But one of the problems we have in the military is we’re in a lot of places around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I mentioned one, and that’s the Balkans.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would very much like to get our troops out of there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I recognize we can’t do it now, nor do I advocate an immediate withdrawal.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That would be an abrogation of our agreement with NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No one is suggesting that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I think it ought to be one of our priorities to work with our European friends to convince them to put troops on the ground.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And there is an example.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Haiti is another example.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now there are some places where I think — you know, I’ve supported the administration in Columbia.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s important for us to be training Columbians in that part of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The hemisphere is in our interest to have a peaceful Columbia.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But —

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think so.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think what we need to do is convince people who live in the lands they live in to build the nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Maybe I’m missing something here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, we’re going to have kind of a nation building core from America?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely not.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our military is meant to fight and win war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what it’s meant to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And when it gets overextended, morale drops.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I strongly believe we need to have a military presence in the Korean peninsula, not only to keep the peace in the peninsula, but to keep regional stability.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I strongly believe we need to keep a presence in NATO, but I’m going to be judicious as to how to use the military.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It needs to be in our vital interest, the mission needs to be clear, and the extra strategy obvious.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t disagree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I certainly don’t disagree that we ought to get our troops home from places like the Balkans as soon as we can, as soon as the mission is complete.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That’s what we did in Haiti.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: There are no more than a handful of American military personnel in Haiti now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And Haitians have their problems, but we gave them a chance to restore democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That’s really about all we can do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But if you have a situation like that right in our backyard with chaos about to break out and flotillas forming to come across the water, and all kinds of violence there, right in one of our neighboring countries there, then I think that we did the right thing there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And as for this idea of nation building, the phrase sounds grandiose.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, we can’t be — we can’t allow ourselves to get overextended.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I certainly agree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I’ve supported building up our capacity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’ve devoted in the budget I’ve proposed, as I said last week, more than twice as much as the governor has proposed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that it’s in better shape now than he generally does.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had some disagreements about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He said that two divisions would have to report not ready for duty, and that’s not what the joint chiefs say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But there’s no doubt that we have to continue building up readiness and military strength.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And we have to also be very cautious in the way we use our military.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I mentioned Third World debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s a place where we can use our generosity to influence in a positive way, influence nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe we ought to have foreign aid, but I don’t think we ought to just have foreign aid for the sake of foreign aid.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think foreign aid needs to be used to encourage markets and reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think a lot of times we just spend aid and say we feel better about it and it ends up being spent the wrong way, and there’s some pretty egregious examples recently.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One being Russia, where we had IMF loans that ended up in the pockets of a lot of powerful people and didn’t help the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the IMF has got a role in the world, but I don’t want to see the IMF out there as a way to say to world bankers, if you make a bad loan, we’ll bail you out.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It needs to be available for emergency situations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I thought the President did the right thing with Mexico and was very strongly supportive of the administration in Mexico.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t think the IMF ought to be a stop loss for people who ought to be able to evaluate risks themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I’ll look at every place where we’re investing money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just want to make sure the return is good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: No, I would make some changes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think there need to be reforms in the IMF.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’ve generally supported it, but I’ve seen them make some calls that I thought were highly questionable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I think that there’s a general agreement in many parts of the world now that there ought to be changes in the IMF.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The World Bank I think is generally doing a better job, but I think one of the big issues here that doesn’t get nearly enough attention is the issue of corruption.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor mentioned it earlier.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’ve worked on this issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s an enormous problem and corruption in official agencies, like militaries and police departments around the world, customs officials, that’s one of the worst forms of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And we have got to again lead by example and help these other countries that are trying to straighten out their situations find the tools in order to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I just think, Jim, that this is an absolutely unique period in world history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The worldâ€™s coming together, as I said, they’re looking to us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And we have a fundamental choice to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Are we going to step up to the plate as a nation the way we did after World War II, the way that generation of heroes said okay, the United States is going to be the leader.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the world benefitted tremendously from the courage that they showed in those post-war years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that in the aftermath of the Cold War, it’s time for us to do something very similar, to step up to the plate, to provide the leadership on the environment, leadership to make sure the world economy keeps moving in the right direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Again, that means not running big deficits here and not squandering our surplus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It means having intelligent decisions that keep our prosperity going and shepherds that economic strength so that we can provide that leadership role.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me comment on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not so sure the role of the United States is to go around the world and say this is the way it’s got to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And maybe it’s just our difference in government, the way we view government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to empower the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to help people help themselves, not have government tell people what to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just don’t think it’s the role of the United States to walk into a country and say, â€œwe do it this way, so should you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: â€ I think we can help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know we’ve got to encourage democracy in the marketplaces.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But take Russia, for example.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We went into Russia, we said here is some IMF money, and it ended up in Viktor Chemomyrdin’s pocket, and others, and yet we played like there was reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The only people that are going to reform Russia are Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re going to have to make the decision themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Putin is going to have to make the decision as to whether or not he wants to adhere to rule of law and normal accounting practices so that if countries and/or entities invest capital, there’s a reasonable rate of return, a way to get the money out of the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But Russia has to make the decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can work with them on security matters, for example, but it’s their call to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I’m not exactly sure where the vice president is coming from, but I think one way for us to end up being viewed as the ugly American is for us to go around the world saying, â€œwe do it this way, so should you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: â€ Now, we trust freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We know freedom is a powerful, powerful, powerful force, much bigger than the United States of America, as we saw recently in the Balkans.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But maybe I misunderstand where you’re coming from, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President, but I think the United States must be humble and must be proud and confident of our values, but humble in how we treat nations that are figuring out how to chart their own course.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Far be it from me to suggest otherwise.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I would.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The only thing an executive order can accomplish is to ban it in federal law enforcement agencies, but I would also support a law in the Congress that would have the effect of doing the same thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I just — I think that racial profiling is a serious problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I remember when the stories first came out about the stops in New Jersey by the highway patrol there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I know it’s been going on a long time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In some ways this is just a new label for something that has been going on for years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I have to confess that it was the first time that I really focused on it in a new way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I was surprised at the extent of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I think we’ve now got so many examples around the country that we really have to find ways to end this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Imagine what it — what it is like for someone to be singled out unfairly, unjustly, and feel the unfair force of law simply because of race or ethnicity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, that runs counter to what the United States of America is all about at our core.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And it’s not an easy problem to solve.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But if I am entrusted with the presidency, it will be the first Civil Rights Act of the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, I can’t imagine what it would be like to be singled out because of race and stopped and harassed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s just flat wrong, and that’s not what America is all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so we ought to do everything we can to end racial profiling.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One of my concerns, though, is I don’t want to federalize the local police forces.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to — obviously in the egregious cases we need to enforce civil rights law, but we need to make sure that internal affairs divisions at the local level do their job and be given a chance to do their job.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe in local control of governments, and obviously if they don’t there needs to be a consequence at the federal level.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it’s very important that we not overstep our bounds and I think most people — most police officers are good, dedicated, honorable citizens who are doing their job, putting their lives at risk who aren’t bigoted or aren’t prejudiced.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think they ought to be held guilty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I do think we need to find out where racial profiling occurs and do something about it and say to the local folks, get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if you can’t, there will be a federal consequence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yeah.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I would agree.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I also agree that most police officers, of course, are doing a good job and hate this practice also.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I talked to an African-American police officer in Springfield, Massachusetts not long ago who raised this question and said that in his opinion one of the biggest solutions is in the training.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And not only the training in police procedures, but human relations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I think that racial profiling is part of a larger issue of how we deal with race in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And as for singling people out because of race, you know, James Byrd was singled out because of his race in Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And other Americans have been singled out because of their race or ethnicity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I think we can embody our values by passing a hate crimes law.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think these crimes are different.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think they’re different because they’re based on prejudice and hatred, which gives rise to crimes that have not just a single victim, but they’re intended to stigmatize and dehumanize a whole group of people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, I don’t, really.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got one in Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And guess what?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The three men who murdered James Byrd, guess what’s going to happen to them?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re going to be put to death.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A jury found them guilty.

transcript_turns.text: My friend, Senator Spencer Abraham of Michigan, is pushing a law to make sure that Arab-Americans are treated with respect.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s the very few that create most of the crises, and we just have to find them and deal with them.

transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you where the biggest discrimination comes.

transcript_turns.text: She’s right.

transcript_turns.text: It starts with making sure every child learns to read.

transcript_turns.text: We can close an achievement gap, and it starts with making sure we have strong accountability, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I believe the federal government must say that if you receive any money, any money from the federal government for disadvantaged children, for example, you must show us whether or not the children are learning.

transcript_turns.text: And I’m going to make it a priority.

transcript_turns.text: One of the reasons we have an instant background check is so that we instantly know whether or not somebody should have a gun or not.
