transcript_turns.text: And that’s what needs to happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got laws.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If laws need to be strengthened, like instant background checks, that’s important.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’ve got a plan to do something about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s to make health care affordable and available this way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First, there’s some who should be buying health care who choose not to.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s some —

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Some of the healthy folks, healthy young kids say I’ll never get sick, therefore I don’t need health care right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For those what I think we need to do is to develop an investment-type vehicle that would be an incentive for them to invest, like medical savings accounts with rollover capacity.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In other words, you say to a youngster, it will be in your financial interest to start saving for future illness, but for the working folks that do want to have health care that can’t afford it, a couple of things we need to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One, we need more community health centers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve developed — put out money in my budget to expand community health centers all around the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: These are places where people can get primary care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly — and they’re good.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re very important parts of the safety net of health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, that you get a $2,000 rebate from the government if you’re a family of $30,000 or less — it scales down as you get higher — that you can use to purchase health care in the private markets.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It will be a huge down payment for a pretty darn good system.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you allow — also allow — convince states to — allow states to allow the mother to match some of the children’s health insurance money with it, the pool purchasing power.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And to make health care more affordable, allow business associations like the National Federal of Independent Business or the Chamber of Commerce or the National Restaurant Association to write association plans across jurisdictional lines so that small businesses have got the capacity to have national pooling to drive the cost of insurance down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s the very best way to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It empowers people, it trusts people, it makes — and it’s a practical way to encourage people to purchase health care insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s one of my top priorities, Jim, to give every single child in the United States affordable health care within the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I would like to see eventually in this country some form of universal health care, but I’m not for a government-run system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In fact, I’m for shrinking the size of government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want a smaller and smarter government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have been in charge of this reinventing government streamlining project that’s reduced the size of government by more than 300,000 people in the last several years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the budget plan that I’ve put out, according to the “Los Angeles Times” again, the way these things are typically measured as a percentage of the GDP, will bring government spending down to the lowest level in 50 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So I want to proceed carefully to cover more people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I think we should start by greatly expanding the so-called child health insurance or CHIP program to give health insurance to every single child in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s intolerable that we have so many millions of children without any health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So it’s one of my top priorities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, I know that we have some disagreements on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I’m sorry to tell you that, you know, there is a record here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And Texas ranks 49th out of the 50 states in health care — in children with health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 49th for women with health care, and 50th for families with health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So it is a priority for me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I guarantee you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m not aware of any program — well, I’ll just leave it at that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think it ought to be a top priority.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First of all, let me say he’s not for a government-run health care system?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I thought that’s exactly what he and Mrs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Clinton and them fought for in 1993 was a government-run health care system.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was fortunately stopped in its tracks.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, we spend $4.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 7 billion a year on the uninsured in the State of Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our rate of uninsured, the percentage of uninsured in Texas has gone down, while the percentage of uninsured in America has gone up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our CHIPS program got a late start because our government meets only four months out of every two years, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It may come as a shock for somebody who has been in Washington for so long.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But actually limited government can work in the second largest state in the union.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And therefore Congress passes the bill after our session in 1997 ended, we passed an enabling legislation in 1999.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve signed up over 110,000 children to the CHIPS program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For comparable states our size, we’re signing them up as fast as any other state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can quote all the numbers you want, but I’m telling you we care about our people in Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We spent a lot of money to make sure people get health care in the State of Texas, and we’re doing a better job than they are at the national level for reducing uninsured.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, I don’t know about all these percentages that he throws out, but I do know that — I speculate that the reason why he didn’t answer your question directly as to whether my numbers were right, the facts were right about Texas ranking dead last in families with health insurance and 49th out of 50 for both children and women, is because those facts are correct.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And as for why it happened, I’m no expert on the Texas procedures, but what my friends there tell me is that the governor opposed a measure put forward by Democrats in the legislature to expand the number of children that would be covered.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And instead directed the money toward a tax cut, a significant part of which went to wealthy interests.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He declared the need for a new tax cut for the oil companies in Texas an emergency need, and so the money was taken away from the CHIP program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: There’s — you don’t have to take my word for this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: There is now a federal judge’s opinion about the current management of this program ordering the State of Texas to do — you should read that judge’s language about this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I believe there are 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 4 million children in Texas who do not have health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 600,000 of whom, and maybe some of those have since gotten it, but as of a year ago 600,000 of them were actually eligible for it but they couldn’t sign up for it because of the barriers that they had set up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If he’s trying to allege that I’m a hard-hearted person and I don’t care about children, he’s absolutely wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve spent $4.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 7 billion a year in the State of Texas for uninsured people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And they get health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, it’s not the most efficient way to get people health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I want to remind you, the number of uninsured in America during their watch has increased.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He can make any excuse he wants, but the facts are that we’re reducing the number of uninsured percentage of our population.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And as the percentage of the population is increasing nationally, somehow the allegation that we don’t care and we’re going to give money for this interest or that interest and not for children in the State of Texas is totally absurd.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me just tell you who the jury is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The people of Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s only been one governor ever elected to back-to-back four-year terms, and that was me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I was able to do so with a lot of Democrat votes, nearly 50% of the Hispanic vote, about 27% of the African-American vote, because people know I’m a conservative person and a compassionate person.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So he can throw all the kinds of numbers around.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m just telling you our state comes together to do what is right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We come together both Republicans and Democrats.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Yes, yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But it’s not a statement about his heart.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t claim to know his heart.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think he’s a good person.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I make no allegations about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I believe him when he says that he has a good heart.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I know enough about your story to admire a lot of the things that you have done as a person.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I think it’s about his priorities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And let me tell you exactly why I think that the choice he made to give a tax cut for the oil companies and others before addressing this — I mean, if you were the governor of a state that was dead last in health care for families, and all of a sudden you found yourself with the biggest surplus your state had ever had in its history, wouldn’t you want to maybe use some of it to climb from 50th to, say, 45 or 40 or something or maybe better?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I would.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, but here is why it’s directly relevant, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because by his own budget numbers, his proposals for spending on tax cuts for the wealthiest of the wealthy are more than the new spending proposals that he has made for health care and education and national defense all combined.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: According to his own numbers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So it’s not a question of his heart, as far as I know.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s a question of priorities and values.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: See, you know —

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First of all, that’s simply not true what he just said, of course.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And secondly, I repeat to you —

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That we spent — the top 1% receive 223 as opposed to 445 billion in new spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The top — let’s talk about my tax plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The top 1% will pay one-third of all the federal income taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And in return, get one-fifth of the benefits, because most of the tax reductions go to the people at the bottom end of the economic ladder.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That stands in stark contrast, by the way, to a man who is going to leave 50 million — 50 million Americans out of tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We just have a different point of view.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a totally different point of view.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He believes only the right people ought to get tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe everybody who pays taxes ought to get tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me go back to Texas, for example, for a minute.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We pay 4.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 7 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I can’t emphasize to you how much.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I signed a bill that puts CHIPS in place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The bill finally came out at the end of the 1999 session.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re working hard to sign up children.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re doing it faster than any other state our size, comparable state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re making really good progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And our state cares a lot about our children.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My priority is going to be the health of our citizens.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: These folks have had eight years to get something done in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: on the uninsured.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They have not done it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’ve had eight years to get something done on Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And they have not got it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And my case to the American people is, if you’re happy with inactivity, stay with the horse.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The horse is up here now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But if you want change, you need to get somebody that knows how to bring Republicans and Democrats together to get positive things done for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that in this 21st century we will soon see the consequences of what’s called global warming.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: There was a study just a few weeks ago suggesting that in summertime the north polar ice cap will be completely gone in 50 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Already many people see the strange weather conditions that the old timers say they’ve never seen before in their lifetimes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And what’s happening is the level of pollution is increasing significantly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, here is the good news, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If we take the leadership role and build the new technologies, like the new kinds of cars and trucks that Detroit is itching to build, then we can create millions of good new jobs by being first into the market with these new kinds of cars and trucks and other kinds of technologies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You know the Japanese are breathing down our necks on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They’re moving very rapidly because they know that it is a fast-growing world market.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Some of these other countries, particularly in the developing world, their pollution is much worse than anywhere else and their people want higher standards of living.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And so they’re looking for ways to satisfy their desire for a better life and still reduce pollution at the same time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that holding onto the old ways and the old argument that the environment and the economy are in conflict is really outdated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have to be bold.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have to provide leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now it’s true that we disagree on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor said that he doesn’t think this problem is necessarily caused by people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He’s for letting the oil companies into the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Houston has just become the smoggiest city in the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And Texas is number one in industrial pollution.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have a very different outlook.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll tell you this, I will fight for a clean environment in ways that strengthen our economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me start with Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We are a big industrial state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We reduced our industrial waste by 11%.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We cleaned up more brown fields than any other administration in my state’s history, 450 of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our water is cleaner now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A brown field is an abandoned industrial site that just sits idle in some of our urban centers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And people are willing to invest capital in the brown fields don’t want to do so for fear of lawsuit.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to have federal liability protection, depending upon whether or not standards have been met.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The book you mentioned that Vice President Gore wrote, he also called for taxing — big energy taxes in order to clean up the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And now that the energy prices are high, I guess he’s not advocating those big energy taxes right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe we ought to fully fund the Land and Water Conservation Fund to — with half the money going to states so states can make the right decisions for environmental quality.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we need to have clean coal technologies.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I propose $2 billion worth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: By the way, I just found out the other day an interesting fact, that there is a national petroleum reserve right next to — in Prudhoe Bay that your administration opened up for exploration in that pristine area.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it was a smart move because there’s gas reserves up there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need gas pipelines to bring the gas down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Gas is a clean fuel that we can burn to — we need to make sure that if we decontrol our plants that there’s mandatory — that the plants must conform to clean air standards, the grandfathered plants, that’s what we did in Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No excuses.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You must conform.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In other words, there are practical things we can do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it starts with working in a collaborative effort with states and local folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you own the land, every day is Earth Day.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People care a lot about their land and care about their environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Not all wisdom is in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: on this issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m really strongly committed to clean water and clean air, and cleaning up the new kinds of challenges like global warming.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He is right that I’m not in favor of energy taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I am in favor of tax cuts to encourage and give incentives for the quicker development of these new kinds of technologies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And let me say again, Detroit is rearing to go on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We differ on the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, as I have said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We differ on whether or not pollution controls ought to be voluntary.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think you can — I don’t think you can get results that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We differ on the kinds of appointments that we would make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s a fundamental difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let me give you an example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Okay, sure.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I don’t believe in command and control out of Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe Washington ought to set standards, but again I think we ought to be collaborative at the local levels and I think we ought to work with people at the local levels.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And by the way, I just want to make sure — I can’t let him just say something and not correct it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The electric decontrol bill that I fought for and signed in Texas has mandatory emission standards, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what we ought to do at the federal level when it comes to grandfathered plants for utilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think there’s a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think, for example, take — when they took 40 million acres of land out of circulation without consulting local officials, I thought that was —

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Out in the west, yeah.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so — on the logging issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the way I would have done it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Perhaps some of that land needs to be set aside.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I certainly would have consulted with governors and elected officials before I would have acted unilaterally.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Sure, absolutely, so long as they’re based upon science and they’re reasonable.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So long as people have input.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s an issue that we need to take very seriously.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t think we know the solution to global warming yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t think we’ve got all the facts before we make decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I tell you one thing I’m not going to do is I’m not going to let the United States carry the burden for cleaning up the world’s air.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Like Kyoto Treaty would have done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: China and India were exempted from that treaty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we need to be more even-handed, as evidently 99 senators — I think it was 99 senators supported that position.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 99 to nothing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, that vote wasn’t exactly — a lot of the supporters of the Kyoto Treaty actually ended up voting for that because the way it was worded.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But there’s no doubt there’s a lot of opposition to it in the Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m not for command and control techniques either.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m for working with the groups, not just with industry but also with the citizen groups and local communities to control sprawl in ways that the local communities themselves come up with.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I disagree that we don’t know the cause of global warming.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s pollution, carbon dioxide, and other chemicals that are even more potent, but in smaller quantities, that cause this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Look, the world’s temperature is going up, weather patterns are changing, storms are getting more violent and unpredictable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: What are we going to tell our children?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m a grandfather now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to be able to tell my grandson when I’m in my later years that I didn’t turn away from the evidence that showed that we were doing some serious harm.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In my faith tradition, it is — it’s written in the book of Matthew, “Where your heart is, there is your treasure also.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: ” And I believe that — that we ought to recognize the value to our children and grandchildren of taking steps that preserve the environment in a way that’s good for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, I agree.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just — I think there has been — some of the scientists, I believe, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President, haven’t they been changing their opinion a little bit on global warming?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A profound scientist recently made a different —

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been trying so hard not to.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Twice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That’s an interruption, by the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I apologize, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Of course they care about them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Oh, you mean the rules.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What the heck.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I — of course there’s a lot — look, global warming needs to be taken very seriously, and I take it seriously.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But science, there’s a lot — there’s differing opinions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And before we react, I think it’s best to have the full accounting, full understanding of what’s taking place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think to answer your question, I think both of us care a lot about the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We may have different approaches.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We may have different approaches in terms of how we deal with local folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just cited an example of the administration just unilaterally acting without any input.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I remember you gave a very good answer to New Hampshire about the White Mountains, about how it was important to keep that collaborative effort in place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I feel very strongly the same place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It certainly wasn’t the attitude that took place out west, however.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, we all make mistakes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been known to mangle a syl-a-ble or two myself, you know, if you know what I mean.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think credibility is important.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is going to be important for the president to be credible with Congress, important for the president to be credible with foreign nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And yes, I think it’s something that people need to consider.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This isn’t something new.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I read a report, or a memo, from somebody in his 1988 campaign — I forgot the fellow’s name — warning then Senator Gore to be careful about exaggerating claims.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I thought during his debate with Senator Bradley saying he authored the EITC when it didn’t happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mention the last debate —

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Earned Income Tax Credit, sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A lot of initials from a guy who’s not from Washington, isn’t it?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Anyway, he co-sponsored McCain-Feingold, and yet he didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I think this is an issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I found it to be an issue in trying to defend my tax relief package.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I thought there was some exaggerations about the numbers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the people are going to have to make up their mind on this issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I am going to continue to defend my record and defend my propositions against what I think are exaggerations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Exaggerations like, for example, only 5% of seniors receive benefits under my Medicare reform package.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what he said the other day, and that’s simply not the case.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I have every right in the world to defend my record and positions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what debates are about and that’s what campaigns are about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I got some of the details wrong last week in some of the examples that I used, Jim, and I’m sorry about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I’m going to try to do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: One of the reasons I regret it is that getting a detail wrong interfered several times with the point that I was trying to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: However many days that young girl in Florida stood in her classroom, however long, even if it was only one day, doesn’t change the fact that there are a lot of overcrowded classrooms in America and we need to do something about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: There are seniors who pay more for their prescriptions than a lot of other people, more than their pets, sometimes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: More sometimes than people in foreign countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And we need to do something about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Not with the measure that leaves the majority of them without any real basic help until the next president’s term of four years is over.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But right away.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And that means doing it under the Medicare program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I can’t promise that I will never get another detail wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I can promise you that I will try not to, and hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I will promise you this with all the confidence in my heart and in the world, that I will do my best if I’m elected president, I’ll work my heart out to get the big things right for the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s going to be up to the people, isn’t it?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Depends on what he says in the future in the campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hope they’re not awful things.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think they may be using the man’s own words.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe I’ve used those words.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Maybe they have.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Wait a minute.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t use language like that and I don’t think that we should.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The — I haven’t seen that, in my commercials?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You haven’t seen the commercial?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that what — I think the point of that is that anybody would have a hard time trying to make a tax cut plan that is so large, that would put us into such big deficits, that gives almost half the benefits to the wealthiest of the wealthy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think anybody would have a hard time explaining that clearly in a way that makes sense to the average person.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s the kind of exaggeration I was just talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, I wasn’t the one having trouble explaining it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Jim, one of the issues that I would like to close with in my statement is education, because it’s an example of the overall approach that I think is important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: This race is about values, it’s about change, it’s about giving choices to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And education is my number one priority, because I think that it’s the most important big major change that we can bring in our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I agree with Governor Bush that we should have new accountability, testing of students.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that we should require states to test all students, test schools and school districts, and I think that we should go further and require teacher testing for new teachers also.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The difference is that while my plan starts with new accountability and maintains local control, it doesn’t stop there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because I want to give new choices to parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: To send their kids to college with a $10,000 tax deduction for college tuition per child per year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to reduce the size of the classrooms in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: For one basic reason, so that students can get more one-on-one time with teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the way to do that is first to recruit more teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’ve a plan in my budget to recruit 100,000 new, highly qualified teachers and to help local school districts build new schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that we have to put more emphasis on early learning and pre-school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, here is how that connects with all the rest of what we’ve been talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you have — if you squander the surplus on a huge tax cut that goes mostly to those at the top, then you can’t make education the top priority.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If the tax cut is your number one, two, three and four priority, you can’t do education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You can’t do both.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You have to choose.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I choose education and health care, the environment and retirement security, and I ask for your support.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Jim, thank you very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President, thank you very much, and I would like to thank the folks here at Wake Forest, and I want to thank you all for listening.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m running to get some things done for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s too many issues left unresolved.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s been too much finger pointing and too much name calling in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would like to unite this country to get an agenda done that will speak to the hopes and aspirations of the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to have an education system that sets high standards, local control of schools and strong accountability.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No child should be left behind in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure we rebuild our military to keep the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I worry about morale in today’s military.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The warning signs are clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is time to have a new commander in chief who will rebuild the military, pay our men and women more, make sure they’re housed better and have a focused mission for our military.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Once and for all, I want to do something about Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This issue has been too long on the table because it’s been a political issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time to bring folks together to say that all seniors will get prescription drug coverage.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to do something about Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s an important priority, because now is the time to act and we’re going to say to our seniors, our promises we’ve made to you will be promises kept.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But younger workers, in order to make sure the system exists tomorrow, younger workers ought to be able to take some of your own money and invest it in safe securities to get a better rate of return on that money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And finally, I do believe in tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe we can set our priorities.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe, like the vice president does, in huge government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe in limited government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: By having a limited government and a focused government, we can send some of the money back to the people who pay the bills.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to have tax relief for all people who pay the bills in America, because I think you can spend your money more wisely than the federal government can.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you for listening.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m asking for your vote, and God bless.
